small_guidance:
- Increase P_BLOCK to 128 or 256 and try OC_BLOCK=32 with num_warps=8 to amortize the heavy nested static_range loops; current 16x64 tile is too small given the inner loop cost (IC*KH*KW*POOL*POOL = 8*3*3*4*4 = 1152 mac iters per element).
- Add a triton.autotune over (OC_BLOCK, P_BLOCK, num_warps, num_stages) ∈ {(16,128,4,2),(32,128,8,2),(32,64,8,3),(64,64,8,2)} keyed on (OC, PH*PW); also try num_stages=3 to overlap the long static-unrolled mac chain.
- Cache input rows: reorder loops so kh/kw are inner and reuse xv across oc tile (already vectorized over oc); consider hoisting bias add and inv_pool2 multiplication outside the dy/dx loop (multiply pooled sum once at the end instead of per-window).
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an im2col-style implicit GEMM: one program per (N, OC tile, OH×OW tile) computing conv directly over the OH×OW grid, then do a second small fused pass (or in-kernel reduction) that sums sigmoid(avg_pool(conv)) into the per-N scalar. Current kernel recomputes overlapping conv outputs across pooled positions only when KH>POOL stride, but mainly suffers from low arithmetic intensity per program; an implicit GEMM with BLOCK_M=64 (OC), BLOCK_N=64 (spatial), BLOCK_K=IC*KH*KW=72 unrolled gives a real matmul shape that tensor-cores/FMA pipelines handle well.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) layout for x and weight reshaped to (OC, IC*KH*KW); IC=8, KH*KW=9 → K=72 fits in one K-tile, so the kernel becomes a single tl.dot per (M,N) tile with no K-loop. Fuse avg-pool as a 4x4 sum-reduction in registers over the spatial tile (size BLOCK_N chosen as multiple of 16 = 4*4 pooled cells) and apply sigmoid + tl.sum into an atomic add on out[n].
- Make the kernel persistent over N (one program per (OC tile, pooled-spatial tile) looping over N) so weights stay resident in registers/SMEM across batch, since OC*IC*KH*KW*4 = 64*72*4 = ~18KB easily fits; this eliminates redundant weight loads which currently dominate given the unrolled tl.load(w) in the innermost loop.
